The Most Underrated Lean Tool? The Spaghetti Diagram.

In a world full of complex frameworks, dashboards, and analytics…
one of the most powerful Lean tools is still a simple drawing.

The Spaghetti Diagram.

And yet, many people underestimate it.



Why?

Because it looks too simple.

No software.
No KPIs.
No complexity.

So people assume:

“This won’t tell us anything new.”

Until they use it.



What makes it powerful

The Spaghetti Diagram does something data often cannot:

👉 It shows reality
👉 It makes waste visible
👉 It creates instant understanding

You don’t need perfect data.

You need:

* A layout
* A pen
* And the willingness to observe what actually happens



The moment that changes everything

You map the movement:

* People
* Materials
* Information

And suddenly…

Lines everywhere.
Crossing. Backtracking. Chaos.

Like a plate of spaghetti.

That’s when it clicks.

Because for the first time, the team doesn’t discuss waste…

They see it.



Real impact (from my projects)

Behind this simple tool, there are real results:

* 🔻 Walking distance reduced by 35–65%
* 🔻 Operator movement reduced by up to 50%
* 🔻 Process steps reduced by 20–40%
* 🔻 Lead time improved by 25–45%
* 🔻 Non-value-added motion cut by >50%

In one case:
👉 Operator walking 8+ km per shift
👉 Reduced to <3 km

Same people. Same process.
Just better flow.



Why it works

Humans understand visuals faster than numbers.

A KPI won’t create urgency.
A chaotic flow on paper will.

It removes opinions.
It removes assumptions.

It shows:

“This is what is really happening.”



What it reveals

Almost every time:

* Unnecessary motion
* Poor layout
* Hidden rework loops
* Lack of standardization
* “Temporary” fixes that became permanent

And the best part?

👉 The team sees it themselves.



The real value

It’s not the drawing.

It’s:

* The discussion it creates
* The awareness it builds
* The mindset shift it triggers

Because once people see it…

They cannot “unsee” it.

No complexity.
No excuses.

Just reality.

If I was setting up LinkedIn outbound from scratch today, here's exactly how I'd build it.

7 patterns Expandi found across 100,000+ conversations from top-performing campaigns:

1. Keep messages short

Under 150 characters lifts replies by 22%.
Cut every word not doing work.

2. Always follow up

Sequences with 2+ follow-ups book 42% more replies than single-shot DMs.
One-shot outbound leaves meetings on the table.

3. Warm the prospect before the ask

Connection requests sent right after a profile view, a like, or a follow hit 30% higher acceptance.
Show up on their radar before you slide into their DMs.

4. Write like a peer, not a pitch

The 4 conversational openers that win:

→ Peer comparison: "We dug into {finding}, want to see what's working for others in {industry}?" (+27% replies)

→ Job change: "Saw you joined {company}, how's {initiative} going?" (+21% replies)

→ Post reference: "Spotted your post on {pain point}, how are you tackling it?" (+19% replies)

→ Trigger-based: "Noticed you're hiring for {roles}, happy with your {topic} setup?" (+18% replies)

5. Personalize every message

Tailored copy lifts replies by 54%.
The extra minutes always pay back.

6. Don't bet everything on LinkedIn

Following up via cold email boosts reply rates by 13%.
Outbound performs best multi-channel.

7. Always have a real reason to reach out

Referencing recent activity (a post, a role change, a new hire) drives 18% more replies.
Generic outreach gets ignored.

→ Benchmarks worth tracking:

Acceptance rate: 40%+
Reply rate: 18%+
Positive reply rate: 8%+

→ The stack we run on:

Expandi for sequencing
Clay for intent and enrichment
Sales Navigator for targeting
Zapier, n8n to wire it all together

Linkedin content creation tools are getting SCARY good at helping you write content (and I truly think some of them are really impressive!)

And once you have great content going out consistently, the next question becomes: WHY do some posts drive more pipeline than others?

- Which posts actually influenced leads
- Which topics consistently drive demo calls
- Which content brought in pipeline vs just impressions

*this is the layer that turns content into a feedback loop (see image below)

Because the writing part is solved (or at least way easier than it used to be), but the post-publish side is still mostly guesswork...you write, you post, you see likes and comments, and then you assume what worked based on engagement alone

And engagement is not the same as business impact

So the flow I think (and I've been dogfooding Socialeads.io for 5 months now) works better, looks like something like this:

1/ Use your favorite Linkedin writing or ideation tool to create content
2/ Connect Socialeads to see what happens after the post goes live
3/ Feed that data back into your content decisions (so you're optimizing for pipeline growth instead of just reactions)

This turns Linkedin content into something closer to a campaign with measurable downstream performance (same as what Fibbler does for ads, now you can see the same conversion metrics for any organic post!)

Because now you're not just posting and hoping...you're posting, tracking, and improving based on what actually moves the people to go and sign up for your... whatever you are offering :)

The whole point is to understand not just that the content worked, but WHY it worked...so you know which hooks, ideas and formats those tools generate actually drive business results (beyond the great engagement they're already getting you!)

- Which topics consistently influence pipeline?
- Which formats drive more signups, demo calls, or trials?
- Which hooks bring in leads vs just likes?

If you want to see how this works with your own posts, Socialeads offers 14 days free trial...and you get to see what worked in your last 90 days of content (leads influenced, deals touched, revenue connected)

Supply Chain Grid: Assess Maturity, Unlock Excellence

Many companies talk about Supply Chain maturity, but few have mapped every step required for true transformation. Progress isn’t about gut feel, it’s about continuous assessment across every domain, with practical, measurable actions.

Here’s my go-to reference, a grid (roadmap) that Supply Chain professionals can use to benchmark and drive improvement:

1️⃣ Strategy
🚩Is your strategy documented
🚩Aligned to business goals
🚩 Fully cascaded
🚩Are KPIs reviewed,
🚩Leadership engaged,
🚩Is CI in Supply Chain DNA 

2️⃣ SC Planning
🚩Demand and supply plans sync
🚩Is forecast accuracy measured / used
🚩Is production planning data-driven
🚩Contingency planning in place

3️⃣ Sourcing
🚩Are supplier selection standardized 
Regular supplier performance reviews 
🚩How strong is risk management,
🚩Strategic partnerships and audits routine driving improvement not just compliance

4️⃣ Customer Management
🚩 Is order processing automated
🚩 Customers see real-time order status
🚩Are SLAs meaningful
🚩Do you manage exceptions when things go off track

5️⃣ External Logistics
🚩Do you track carrier qualifications
🚩Shipment visibility
🚩Freight optimization
🚩Transport risks addressed

6️⃣ Internal Logistics
🚩Are internal workflows mapped
🚩Tools like AGVs/RFID deployed
🚩 Bottlenecks analyzed
🚩Staff regularly trained

7️⃣ Warehousing
🚩Are warehouse layouts efficient
🚩Is WMS active
🚩Are cycle counts robust
🚩Picking accuracy tracked
🚩Safety walks punctual

8️⃣ Inventory Management
🚩Is inventory tracked by SKU
🚩Safety stock policy reviewed
🚩 Obsolescence managed
🚩 Physical counts reconciled

9️⃣ Materials Planning
🚩Are requirements model-driven
🚩MRP reviewed
🚩Supplier lead times monitored
🚩Shortages systematically tracked

1️⃣0️⃣ Production
🚩Is schedule adherence a metric
🚩Are quality/yield KPIs, flexibility, and root-cause analysis at the heart of your daily routine

1️⃣1️⃣ Delivery Planning
🚩Is delivery planning integrated
🚩Last-mile tracked, 
🚩Routing/scheduling tools leveraged
🚩Communication seamless

1️⃣2️⃣ Aftermarket, Sustainability
🚩Are returns standardized
🚩Sustainability metrics tracked
🚩Reverse logistics launched, 
🚩Aftermarket waste measured

1️⃣3️⃣ Technology
🚩Are ERP systems deployed
🚩Is data accurate
🚩Dashboards used for decisions
🚩Integration strong
🚩Upgrades routine

1️⃣4️⃣ People & Organization
🚩Are skills matrices standard
🚩R&R defined clearly
🚩Is change management supported
🚩Engagement measured

Every domain offers practical checkpoints, more than theory, they’re action items for building resilient, future-proof supply chains. If you aren’t measuring maturity, you’re missing out full potential of Excellence.

items.content:
I talk to Supply Chain Directors regularly.

One pattern keeps showing up. 
The gap between what they expected from Agentic AI and what actually happened after go-live.

Here's what surprises them most.

1. It works best on repetitive decisions, not strategic ones. 
The biggest wins came from high-volume, rule-based calls. Expedite or not. Allocate or hold. Not from strategy. 
The system handles the noise. People handle the judgment calls.

2. Deployment takes 6–9 months, not 6 weeks.
Vendors promise fast. Reality is slow. 
Change management, data cleanup, process redesign. 
None of that fits in a sprint.

3. The biggest win isn't the outcome. It's decision transparency.
Planners stopped asking "why did the system do that?" They started understanding it. 
Teams work differently once that shift happens.

4. Clean data isn't optional.
Put an agent on top of messy data and you get wrong answers delivered with confidence. 
The AI doesn't know it's wrong. That's the risk.
5. People don't lose their jobs. Their jobs change.
The repetitive part gets automated. 
The judgment part gets more visible, and more accountable.

These are patterns, not laws. I could be wrong on some of them.

Which one matches your reality?
